triggers.explicit: user wording asks for a memory operation, including 'save this so future sessions can retrieve it'
triggers.implicit_write: ordinary conversation reveals a durable fact (stable preference, constraint, identity, project convention, long-term decision/state change, or a complaint revealing a standing rule) — write once in the same turn and acknowledge; host-native memory mechanisms do not substitute
triggers.implicit_read: question or task depends on remembered facts — 'which/what/when + my/our/usual/previous' question forms, plans needing a standing constraint, or actions (install/build/run/commit/history rewrite) a remembered convention could govern (plain task phrasing does not make it memory-independent) — search before answering or acting; query one distinctive constraint attribute term first (the keyword engine ANDs every term, so extra words empty the result); report empty results honestly; skip only when nothing remembered could govern the reply: general technical questions with no user-specific reference; imperative commands whose action and target are already fully specified ('remember to <do X>' with exact parameters — a reminder to act even when it touches git or config files); current-environment content questions (filesystem); and plain environment/tool state work (browser/system cache, IDE window layout, bookmarks, Notion links). A request that must CONSULT a convention before acting ('the way I usually do', under a branch/history policy, choosing names) still searches first
never: conditional what-ifs ('if I switch to X next month' is hypothetical, not a standing fact)
anything derived from a request whose secret payload was declined
facts the user declined to store
third-party facts misattributed to the user

intents.name: write
intents.condition: explicit user intent or implicit durable-fact disclosure

intents.name: ingest
intents.condition: explicit intent + stable session and source IDs
